reason: E4 shows heat treatment promotes short-range order in CrCoNi. E1 and E2 directly state that increased local chemical order narrows interstitial/vacancy mobility, enhances recombination, and delays irradiation damage. However, the hypothesis extrapolates from 'irradiation damage resistance' to 'corrosion resistance' without any cited evidence linking the two, leaving the final premise unsupported.
premises: Short-range ordering (LCO) can be promoted in CrCoNi by heat treatment
LCO narrows the mobility ratio of irradiation-induced interstitials and vacancies
Narrowed mobility ratio enhances point-defect recombination
Enhanced recombination delays irradiation damage initiation
Delayed damage initiation translates to improved corrosion resistance
